name: Holy Basil / Tulsi
description: Tulsi is an aromatic herb widely grown around homes and temples in India. It is highly valued in Ayurveda and Indian cultural traditions.
traditionalUses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic preparations and household herbal practices. It is commonly associated with respiratory and general wellness traditions.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with supporting respiratory comfort, digestion and general wellness.
traditionalUsage: Leaves are commonly used fresh or dried in herbal preparations and traditional beverages.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical regions; commonly cultivated in India.
identification: Aromatic leaves, square stems, opposite leaves and small flowers arranged on spikes.

health.issues: Common issues may include fungal diseases, insect pests or environmental stress.
health.symptoms: Leaf spots, yellowing, wilting or damaged leaves.
health.prevention: Good airflow, suitable watering, healthy soil and removal of severely affected plant material.

name: Neem
description: Neem is a well-known evergreen tree of the Indian subcontinent and has a long history in traditional Indian practices.
traditionalUses: Traditionally used in preparations associated with skin care, hygiene and general wellness.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with skin and oral hygiene practices.
plantPartsTraditionallyUsed: Leaves, bark, seeds, flowers and oil.
traditionalUsage: Leaves and other parts have traditionally been incorporated into herbal preparations and household practices.
habitat: Tropical and semi-arid regions, especially across India.
identification: Large evergreen tree with pinnate leaves and small white fragrant flowers.

health.symptoms: Sticky residue on leaves or stunted growth.
health.prevention: Ensure good drainage and prune dead branches.

name: Aloe Vera
description: Aloe vera is a succulent plant recognized by its thick, fleshy leaves containing clear gel.
traditionalUses: Traditionally used in skin-care preparations and various Ayurvedic and household practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with skin soothing and digestive preparations.
traditionalUsage: The clear inner gel is traditionally applied in certain skin-care preparations.
habitat: Warm, dry and tropical regions.
identification: Thick pointed succulent leaves arranged in a rosette, often with small teeth along the margins.

health.symptoms: Mushy, yellowing leaves at the base.
health.prevention: Plant in well-draining soil and water only when completely dry.

name: Turmeric
description: Turmeric is a rhizomatous plant widely cultivated in South and Southeast Asia.
traditionalUses: A major ingredient in Ayurveda, traditional cuisine and cultural practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestive and general wellness practices.
traditionalUsage: Fresh or dried rhizomes are used as a spice and in traditional preparations.
habitat: Warm, humid tropical regions.
identification: Broad green leaves and underground yellow-orange rhizomes.

health.symptoms: Yellowing of outer leaves and decaying roots.
health.prevention: Avoid waterlogging and use disease-free seed rhizomes.

name: Ginger
description: Ginger is a flowering plant cultivated mainly for its aromatic underground rhizome.
traditionalUses: Widely used in Ayurveda and traditional food and herbal preparations.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestion and relief of occasional digestive discomfort.
traditionalUsage: Fresh or dried ginger is used in food, beverages and traditional preparations.
habitat: Warm tropical and subtropical climates.
identification: Narrow lance-shaped leaves, upright stems and branching aromatic rhizomes.

health.symptoms: Yellowing leaf tips extending downwards; soft foul-smelling rhizomes.
health.prevention: Ensure excellent drainage and crop rotation.

name: Ashwagandha
description: Ashwagandha is a small shrub traditionally important in Ayurveda.
traditionalUses: Traditionally classified as a Rasayana herb and used in various Ayurvedic preparations.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with vitality, strength and general wellness.
plantPartsTraditionallyUsed: Primarily root; leaves and berries are also used in some traditional practices.
traditionalUsage: Roots are traditionally dried and powdered or incorporated into preparations.
habitat: Dry and semi-arid regions.
identification: Small shrub with oval leaves, pale flowers and small orange-red berries.

health.symptoms: Webbing on leaves or brown spotting.
health.prevention: Keep plants well-spaced for airflow and avoid overhead watering.

name: Amla / Indian Gooseberry
description: Amla is a small to medium-sized tree producing greenish-yellow fruits.
traditionalUses: Important in Ayurveda and commonly included in traditional formulations.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestive and general wellness practices.
traditionalUsage: Fruit is eaten fresh, dried or used in traditional preparations.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical parts of India.
identification: Small feathery-looking leaves and round pale-green fruits.

health.symptoms: Webbed frass on branches or rusty spots on leaves.
health.prevention: Prune affected branches and maintain overall tree vigor.

name: Brahmi
description: Brahmi is a small creeping herb commonly found in moist environments.
traditionalUses: Traditionally used in Ayurveda in preparations associated with memory and mental wellness.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with memory, concentration and general nervous-system wellness.
plantPartsTraditionallyUsed: Whole plant, especially leaves and stems.
traditionalUsage: Traditionally prepared as fresh juice, powder or incorporated into herbal formulations.
habitat: Wetlands, marshes, ponds and moist soil.
identification: Small succulent leaves, creeping stems and small white flowers.

health.symptoms: Chewed leaves or dark patches in stagnant water.
health.prevention: Ensure clean water sources and remove excessive decaying organic matter.

name: Sandalwood
description: Sandalwood is a fragrant tree valued for its aromatic heartwood.
traditionalUses: Used in Ayurveda, traditional cosmetics, religious ceremonies and cultural practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with cooling and skin-care preparations.
traditionalUsage: Sandalwood paste and traditionally prepared sandalwood oil are used in cultural and cosmetic practices.
habitat: Tropical regions, especially parts of the Indian subcontinent.
identification: Small evergreen tree with smooth bark and paired oval leaves.

health.symptoms: Reduction in leaf size and stiffening of leaves like spikes.
health.prevention: Remove infected trees immediately as there is no known cure.

name: Moringa / Drumstick
description: Moringa is a fast-growing tree widely cultivated for its edible leaves, flowers and pods.
traditionalUses: Used as food and in traditional wellness practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally valued as a nutritious plant and associated with general wellness.
traditionalUsage: Leaves and pods are commonly cooked as food; leaves may also be used in traditional preparations.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical regions.
identification: Small compound leaves, white flowers and long slender seed pods.

health.symptoms: Defoliation of leaves or sudden wilting.
health.prevention: Manual removal of pests and avoiding waterlogged soil.

name: Curry Leaf
description: Curry leaf is a small aromatic tree whose leaves are widely used in South Asian cuisine.
traditionalUses: Used in food and traditional herbal practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestion and general wellness.
traditionalUsage: Leaves are commonly used fresh in cooking and traditional preparations.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical South Asia.
identification: Pinnate aromatic leaves with many small leaflets.

health.symptoms: Curling of leaves and white powdery residue.
health.prevention: Prune affected areas and maintain good sunlight exposure.

name: Lemongrass
description: Lemongrass is an aromatic grass with a strong lemon-like fragrance.
traditionalUses: Used in herbal beverages, cooking and traditional wellness practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestive comfort and relaxation.
traditionalUsage: Used fresh or dried in herbal teas and food preparations.
habitat: Warm tropical and subtropical regions.
identification: Long narrow grass-like leaves with a strong citrus aroma.

health.symptoms: Brown or rust-colored streaks on leaves.
health.prevention: Harvest regularly and remove old debris to improve airflow.

name: Mint / Pudina
description: Mint is an aromatic herb widely cultivated for its refreshing leaves.
traditionalUses: Used in food, beverages and traditional herbal practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestion and refreshing herbal preparations.
traditionalUsage: Fresh leaves are used in chutneys, drinks, food and herbal preparations.
habitat: Moist soils and cultivated gardens in temperate and subtropical regions.
identification: Opposite aromatic leaves and square stems.

health.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves or curled tips.
health.prevention: Ensure good spacing for airflow and avoid wetting foliage.

name: Hibiscus
description: Hibiscus is a flowering shrub commonly grown in tropical gardens.
traditionalUses: Flowers and leaves have traditional uses in hair-care and cultural practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with hair and skin-care practices.
traditionalUsage: Flowers may be used in traditional hair-care preparations and herbal beverages.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical gardens.
identification: Large showy flowers, broad leaves and a woody shrub form.

health.symptoms: White cottony clusters on stems or sticky leaves.
health.prevention: Regular inspection and removal of heavily infested shoots.

name: Ixora / Jungle Geranium
description: Ixora is an evergreen flowering shrub commonly cultivated as an ornamental plant.
traditionalUses: Certain parts have been used in traditional herbal practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditional systems have associated different plant parts with various wellness preparations.
traditionalUsage: Used traditionally in selected herbal preparations.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical regions.
identification: Dense clusters of small four-petaled flowers and glossy leaves.

health.symptoms: Black powdery coating on leaves.
health.prevention: Control scale insects which secrete the honeydew that mold grows on.

name: Arjuna
description: Arjuna is a large tree well known in Ayurveda.
traditionalUses: The bark is traditionally important in Ayurvedic preparations.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated particularly with cardiovascular wellness.
traditionalUsage: Bark is traditionally dried and used in herbal preparations.
habitat: Often found near rivers and in moist tropical areas of India.
identification: Large tree with smooth grey bark and distinctive buttressed trunk.

health.symptoms: Holes in the bark with frass.
health.prevention: Maintain tree vigor and avoid mechanical injury to the trunk.

name: Licorice / Mulethi
description: Licorice is a perennial herb cultivated for its sweet-tasting root.
traditionalUses: Used traditionally in Ayurveda and other herbal traditions.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with throat comfort and digestive wellness.
traditionalUsage: Dried root is traditionally used in powders, teas and herbal formulations.
habitat: Temperate and subtropical regions.
identification: Compound leaves, pale flowers and underground spreading roots.

health.symptoms: Stunted growth and decaying roots.
health.prevention: Ensure deep, well-draining soil and avoid overwatering.

name: Shatavari
description: Shatavari is a climbing plant with delicate foliage and tuberous roots.
traditionalUses: An important traditional Ayurvedic herb.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with general vitality and women's wellness traditions.
traditionalUsage: Roots are traditionally dried, powdered and used in herbal preparations.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical regions.
identification: Climbing stems with fine needle-like foliage and tuberous roots.

health.symptoms: Orange-red pustules on leaves or wilting vines.
health.prevention: Provide support for climbing to improve airflow and ensure well-draining soil.

name: Giloy
description: Giloy is a climbing medicinal plant traditionally important in Ayurveda.
traditionalUses: Traditionally used in various Ayurvedic herbal preparations.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with general wellness and immune-support traditions.
plantPartsTraditionallyUsed: Stem is the main traditionally used part.
traditionalUsage: Stem is traditionally prepared as decoctions, powders or other herbal preparations.
habitat: Tropical regions of the Indian subcontinent.
identification: Climbing vine with heart-shaped leaves and characteristic aerial roots.

health.symptoms: Occasional leaf-eating caterpillars.
health.prevention: Requires minimal care, naturally resists most common diseases.

name: Vetiver / Khus
description: Vetiver is a perennial grass known for its highly aromatic roots.
traditionalUses: Used in traditional cooling preparations, fragrances and herbal practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with cooling and refreshing applications.
traditionalUsage: Roots are used in traditional aromatic preparations and cooling drinks.
habitat: Tropical regions, especially cultivated in India.
identification: Tall grass forming dense clumps with long narrow leaves and fragrant roots.

health.symptoms: Damage to clumps.
health.prevention: Maintain adequate soil moisture.

name: Black Pepper
description: Black pepper is a climbing vine cultivated for its peppercorns.
traditionalUses: Widely used as a spice and in Ayurveda.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestion and respiratory wellness.
traditionalUsage: Used as a spice and in traditional herbal preparations.
habitat: Warm humid tropical regions, especially Kerala and other parts of South India.
identification: Climbing vine, heart-shaped leaves and hanging spikes of small fruits.

health.symptoms: Sudden yellowing and wilting of the entire vine.
health.prevention: Ensure excellent drainage during monsoons and avoid damaging the base of the vine.

name: Cardamom / Green Cardamom
description: Green cardamom is a perennial herb valued for its aromatic seed pods.
traditionalUses: Used in Ayurveda, cuisine and traditional beverages.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestion and freshening the breath.
traditionalUsage: Used as a spice, in tea and in traditional preparations.
habitat: Humid tropical forests and plantations, especially South India.
identification: Tall leafy shoots with small capsules produced near the base.

health.symptoms: Dead shoots and holes in capsules.
health.prevention: Regular removal of dry leaves and affected shoots.

name: Cinnamon
description: Cinnamon is an evergreen tree cultivated for its aromatic inner bark.
traditionalUses: Used as a spice and in traditional herbal preparations.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestion and warming herbal preparations.
traditionalUsage: Bark is dried and used in food, beverages and herbal preparations.
habitat: Tropical regions, especially South and Southeast Asia.
identification: Evergreen tree with aromatic bark and leathery leaves.

health.symptoms: Brown spots on leaves or damage to the bark.
health.prevention: Ensure good sunlight penetration and airflow.

name: Clove
description: Clove is an evergreen tree whose dried flower buds are used as a spice.
traditionalUses: Used in Ayurveda, cuisine and traditional oral-care practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with oral comfort and digestion.
traditionalUsage: Dried buds are used as a spice and in traditional preparations.
habitat: Tropical humid regions.
identification: Evergreen tree with glossy leaves and clusters of reddish flower buds.

health.issues: Sudden death disease and leaf rot.
health.symptoms: Rapid yellowing and shedding of leaves followed by tree death.
health.prevention: Strictly avoid waterlogging around the root zone.

name: Indian Bay Leaf / Tejpatta
description: Indian bay leaf is an aromatic tree whose leaves are commonly used as a spice.
traditionalUses: Used in Indian cooking and traditional herbal practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestion.
traditionalUsage: Dried leaves are commonly used in cooking and traditional preparations.
habitat: Himalayan and subtropical regions of South Asia.
identification: Aromatic leathery leaves with prominent parallel veins.

health.symptoms: Silvery trails on leaves or small galls.
health.prevention: Remove and destroy heavily infested leaves.

name: Fenugreek / Methi
description: Fenugreek is an annual herb cultivated for its leaves and aromatic seeds.
traditionalUses: Used widely in Indian cooking and traditional herbal practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestion and nutritional wellness.
traditionalUsage: Seeds and leaves are used in food and traditional preparations.
habitat: Cultivated in dry and semi-arid regions.
identification: Three-part leaves, small pale flowers and angular yellow-brown seeds.

health.symptoms: Stunted seedlings or white powder on leaves.
health.prevention: Ensure well-draining soil and avoid dense sowing.

name: Coriander / Cilantro
description: Coriander is an aromatic annual herb used widely as a culinary and traditional plant.
traditionalUses: Used in cooking and traditional herbal practices.
medicinalBenefits: Traditionally associated with digestion and refreshing preparations.
traditionalUsage: Fresh leaves and dried seeds are widely used in food and beverages.
habitat: Cultivated across tropical, subtropical and temperate regions.
identification: Fine divided leaves, small white flowers and round aromatic seeds.

health.symptoms: Curled leaves and swollen stems.
health.prevention: Ensure good spacing and use clean seeds.
